text:
Customer-Jane: hey team — we started seeing intermittent spikes in streaming responses this morning. non-stream (sync) requests look normal, but streaming/ SSE / h2 streams have huge TTFB on p95/p99. around 10-20% of requests get a 300-800ms idle before the first chunk. request id: req_0a1b2c3d; examples attached. can you advise?

Anna (Support): thanks @Customer-Jane — sorry for the trouble. can you paste a raw curl (or trace) you used to reproduce? also which protocol: SSE over http/1.1 or http2? any proxy in front?

Customer-Jane: we use HTTP/2 with chunked responses (server push disabled). curl we used: `curl -v --http2 -N "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream" -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'` — I can repro with `-N`. headers: `te: trailers`, `accept: text/event-stream`. We have an nginx reverse proxy in front of our app and then a load balancer.

Marco (Runtime): thanks for the repro. quick theory: runtime emits small chunks early, but upstream (nginx/lb) or intermediate HTTP/2 layer may coalesce or buffer tiny writes, causing long TTFB on some connections. h2 flow control/windowing + proxy write coalescing can produce sporadic delays. do you have sample server logs for req_0a1b2c3d showing chunk writes?

Customer-Jane: here's a trimmed log snippet for req_0a1b2c3d: 
```
[12:03:21.112] initial request received
[12:03:21.120] model first token generated (0.008s)
[12:03:21.121] write chunk: "data: \u003cfirst\u003e\n\n" (size 18)
[12:03:21.121] flush requested
[12:03:21.420] client ACK/log shows first bytes received (0.299s)
```
so we flush but client doesn't see bytes for ~300ms. other requests show ~20ms as expected.

Eli (Network): that pattern strongly suggests intermediate buffering/coalescing. can you check nginx config for `proxy_buffering`/`proxy_http_version` and whether `proxy_set_header Connection ""` is set? also confirm LB's http2 config — some managed LBs will batch small frames.

Customer-Jane: nginx has default config; i don't see `proxy_buffering off` set.

Anna (Support): ok, preliminary mitigation: try disabling proxy buffering for this endpoint to see if it fixes TTFB. if that's not possible, a runtime change to emit slightly larger first chunks (e.g., pad to ~1KB) has helped other customers temporarily. i can escalate to runtime for a better long-term fix.

Marco (Runtime): agree. long-term we want two mitigations: 1) adaptive-chunking in runtime — coalesce model tokens up to a small threshold (e.g., 512-1024 bytes) or wait X ms (10-30ms) before first flush to avoid tiny writes; 2) add per-connection `TCP_CORK`/ `TCP_NODELAY` heuristics and explicit http2 frame flush hints where supported. short-term: force min-chunk-size = 512 bytes for that customer via a routing rule.

Sam (Oncall): i'm going to pull traces and a packet capture for the request id. @DeployBot can you create a canary config to set min-chunk-size=512 for customer_jane? we should route a small % first.

DeployBot: created canary rollout 42: route 5% of traffic for `customer_jane` to runtime config `min_chunk_bytes=512, initial_flush_delay_ms=20`. start time 12:45 UTC. monitor p95/p99 for 30m.

Sam (Oncall): capture attached shows client-side delays align with proxy responses (we see server FIN/PSH delayed at the proxy side). that confirms buffering at proxy/LB.

Marco (Runtime): because we saw a regression in p99 after last runtime change to aggressively stream tokens (to reduce latency/cost), we've traded off tiny-write frequency vs TTFB outliers. current plan: revert aggressive immediate-flush behavior and roll adaptive-chunking as default with opt-out. i'll prepare a patch.

Eli (Network): note for customers behind nginx: recommend adding per-route config: 
```
location /v1/stream {
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_request_buffering off;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Connection "";
  # optional: sendfile off; tcp_nodelay on;
}
```
for h2 in front, ask LB vendor about minimum frame coalescing windows. some managed LBs have a 100-300ms coalescing behavior for small frames.

Customer-Jane: the canary rollout reduced p99 from ~800ms to ~70ms for the sample traffic we tried. this looks promising. thanks.

Anna (Support): great — action summary:
- Sam: validate canary metrics and upload perf graphs (ETA 1h)
- Marco: open PR for adaptive-chunking with default min_chunk=512 and initial_delay=20ms (ETA EOD)
- Eli: add nginx guidance to docs + contact LB vendor to confirm coalescing behavior (ETA 2d)
- Anna: follow up with customer on config changes and final rollback plan if needed (ETA 2h)

Marco (Runtime): I'll also add a temporary flag to auto-fallback streaming->sync for customers who opt-out until we ship adaptive-chunking. PR will include tests and perf regression guard.

DeployBot: scheduled canary monitor job (job id 9876). alert if stream_ttfb_p99 > 200ms for 5m.

Customer-Jane: thanks all, we'll test more and post results. appreciate the quick triage :thumbsup:

Anna (Support): closing loop once EOD PR merged and customer confirms. leaving thread open for follow-ups.
